title: Topography of mutational signatures in human cancer
authors: Otlu B; Díaz-Gay M; Vermes I; Bergstrom EN; Zhivagui M; Barnes M; Alexandrov LB
one_liner_zh: 该文分析癌症体细胞突变特征与基因组拓扑特征（如核小体、组蛋白修饰）的关联，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract:
SUMMARY

The somatic mutations found in a cancer genome are imprinted by different mutational processes. Each process exhibits a characteristic mutational signature, which can be affected by the genome architecture. However, the interplay between mutational signatures and topographical genomic features has not been extensively explored. Here, we integrate mutations from 5,120 whole-genome sequenced tumours from 40 cancer types with 516 topographical features from ENCODE to evaluate the effect of nucleosome occupancy, histone modifications, CTCF binding, replication timing, and transcription/replication strand asymmetries on the cancer-specific accumulation of mutations from distinct mutagenic processes. Most mutational signatures are affected by topographical features with signatures of related aetiologies being similarly affected. Certain signatures exhibit periodic behaviours or cancer-type specific enrichments/depletions near topographical features, revealing further information about the processes that imprinted them. Our findings, disseminated via COSMIC, provide a comprehensive online resource for exploring the interactions between mutational signatures and topographical features across human cancer.

GRAPHICAL ABSTRACT

HIGHLIGHTS

Comprehensive topography analysis of mutational signatures encompassing 82,890,857 somatic mutations in 5,120 whole-genome sequenced tumours integrated with 516 tissue-matched topographical features from the ENCODE project. The accumulation of somatic mutations from most mutational signatures is affected by nucleosome occupancy, histone modifications, CTCF binding sites, transcribed regions, or replication strand/timing. Mutational signatures with related aetiologies are consistently characterized by similar genome topographies across tissue types. Topography analysis allows both separating signatures from different aetiologies and understanding the genomic specificity of clustered somatic mutations. A comprehensive online resource, disseminate through the COSMIC signatures database, that allows researchers to explore the interactions between somatic mutational processes and genome architecture within and across cancer types.
abstract_zh:
摘要

癌症基因组中发现的体细胞突变受到不同突变过程的印记。每个过程表现出特征性的突变签名，这些签名可能受到基因组结构的影响。然而，突变签名与地形基因组特征之间的相互作用尚未得到广泛探索。在此，我们整合了来自40种癌症类型的5，120个全基因组测序肿瘤中的突变，以及来自ENCODE的516个地形特征，以评估核小体占用、组蛋白修饰、CTCF结合、复制时间以及转录/复制链不对称性对不同致突变过程癌症特异性突变积累的影响。大多数突变签名受到地形特征的影响，且相关病因的签名受到相似影响。某些签名表现出周期性行为或在特定地形特征附近的癌症类型特异性富集/缺失，揭示了印记这些签名的过程的进一步信息。我们的发现通过COSMIC传播，提供了一个全面的在线资源，用于探索人类癌症中突变签名与地形特征之间的相互作用。

图形摘要

亮点

对突变签名的全面地形分析，涵盖5，120个全基因组测序肿瘤中的82，890，857个体细胞突变，并与来自ENCODE项目的516个组织匹配地形特征整合。大多数突变签名的体细胞突变积累受到核小体占用、组蛋白修饰、CTCF结合位点、转录区域或复制链/时间的影响。具有相关病因的突变签名在不同组织类型中一致地表现出相似的基因组地形特征。地形分析允许区分不同病因的签名，并理解聚集体细胞突变的基因组特异性。一个全面的在线资源，通过COSMIC签名数据库传播，使研究人员能够探索癌症类型内部及之间的体细胞突变过程与基因组结构之间的相互作用。
